newsitem.title: USA: House votes to deny extra time for Gingrich probe.
newsitem.headline: House votes to deny extra time for Gingrich probe.

text.p: The House voted Tuesday to deny extra time for the House ethics committee to conclude its work on the investigation of Speaker Newt Gingrich.

The virtual party line vote of 223-205 came less than three hours after Gingrich was re-elected Speaker. Democrats had supported a request by an ethics subcommittee and its special counsel James Cole to go beyond the orginal Jan. 21 date for a House vote on punishment for Gingrich. Republicans opposed the extension.
Cole said in a statement that in analyzing the time needed to conduct a sanction hearing and floor vote "it will be necessary for the vote on the House floor to occur after January 21, 1997."

He said all members of the four-member bipartisan subcommittee had agreed. But when Democrats proposed changing a rule proposed by Republicans that called for House "final disposition" of the Gingrich report at the latest by Jan. 21, Republicans objected.
Ethics Committee member David Hobson, R-Ohio, complained that the Democratic motion, which contained no end-date, meant the affair could "go on for ever and ever."
Republican Leader Dick Armey told reporters, "Cole, the counsel, does not schedule the floor of the House of Representatives."
